newsitem.title: USA: Police optimistic Texas standoff to end peacefully.
newsitem.headline: Police optimistic Texas standoff to end peacefully.

text.p: Negotiations with armed Texas separatists holed up in a mountain compound are going well and authorities are optimistic a three-day standoff will end peacefully, a police spokesman said Tuesday.

"We're optimistic there's going to be a peaceful outcome to all this," Texas Department of Public Safety spokesman Mike Cox told reporters. "We've had a good dialogue going on and things are looking very positive."

Cox said negotiators from the Texas Rangers had been in talks by telephone with Richard McLaren, self-styled "ambassador" for the Republic of Texas group. The group, which has ties to anti-government militias, wants Texas to secede from the United States.

Cox said McLaren told police he wanted to deliver a box of legal documents to his lawyer, Terence O'Rourke, who has been waiting since Monday at a police roadblock to speak with his client. Cox did not disclose what the documents were or what police were negotiating with the group.
"Our discussions have been reasonable, there've been no wild and outlandish threats. Things are really going very well," Cox said.

The standoff began on Sunday when members of the Republic of Texas grabbed two hostages from a nearby home in retaliation for the arrest of their security chief on charges he had illegal weapons. Charges of aggravated kidnapping and engaging in an organized criminal activity were filed against six of the Republic members on Monday.
